title: Perimeter Observability Ingest Sharding for Private Clusters
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a perimeter-level ingest sharding proxy for Private/VPC deployments that provides per-tenant isolation, backpressure handling, and network-segment aware routing. Goal is to reduce noisy-tenant amplification on on-prem collectors, enable soft multi-tenant quotas at the edge, and surface tenant-level tracing hooks before data reaches shared aggregation pipelines. This work covers: design and implementation of an ingest gateway service, routing rules, lightweight tenant admission controls, and compatibility shim for existing on-prem collector agents.
acceptance_criteria: Perimeter ingest gateway deployed as an optional sidecar or standalone HA pair in private control plane and passes canary traffic
Gateway enforces per-tenant soft quotas and returns clear 429 semantics to callers when exceeded
Tenant-level trace headers are preserved and enriched with gateway attributes (node-id, route-shard) before forwarding
Gateway implements at-least-one sharding strategy distributing tenants across collector pools and supports re-sharding without data loss
End-to-end tests validate isolation: noisy tenant synthetic workload does not increase median latency for other tenants by more than 5%
Observability dashboards show gateway ingress QPS, per-tenant error rates, and shard skew metrics and are included in runbook links
comments: 2026-01-30 - Maya Chen: Initial ticket created. Problem observed in private clusters where single tenant spikes cause collector queue saturation and cascade to increased ingestion latency for others. Proposed solution: perimeter ingest shard/gateway to apply soft quotas and route traffic into tenant-bounded collector pools.

2026-02-05 - Arjun Patel: Architecture proposal uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Perimeter+Ingest+Sharding. Key trade-offs: (1) gateway adds an extra network hop and complexity vs direct enforcement in collectors, (2) gateway enables early rejection but duplicates some admission logic. Leaning toward gateway for faster rollout and centralized policy enforcement.

2026-02-12 - SRE review (Liam O'Connor): Raised concern about single-point-of-failure for standalone gateway. Action: implement HA pair with client-side retry/backoff and local fallback path to collectors when gateway unavailable. Added to implementation notes.

2026-02-20 - Design feedback (Priya Rao): UI needs: per-tenant token mapping, shard assignment heatmap, and a per-tenant quota override panel in Console. Created PM ticket to track console changes: PM-1189.

2026-02-28 - Engineering sync: Agreed on sharding algorithm: consistent-hash by tenant-id with periodic bounded re-sharding window. Re-shard plan includes sticky routing for in-flight streams and a graceful TTL-based handoff for KV cache entries. Implementation PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-gateway/pull/156 (WIP).

2026-03-03 - Security review kickoff (Anika Duarte): Gateway will accept tenant-mapped client certs and validate tokens. Need KMS integration for per-tenant secrets; added dependency on KMS team. Threat model doc attached to Confluence page.

2026-03-07 - Load test plan: synthetic traffic generator that simulates 100 tenants with Zipf distribution (alpha=1.2) to validate shard skew and noisy-tenant isolation. Target: gateway can reject or throttle top 5% offending tenants while keeping 95th percentile ingestion latency within SLOs. Results to be uploaded to: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/private/ingest-shard/overview

2026-03-10 - Progress update: Basic gateway binary built with route table, quota logic, and header enrichment. Running integration tests against local collector pool. Next: add graceful re-shard handoff and metrics export for shard skew. Assigned follow-up subtasks: ENG-22148 (integration tests), ENG-22149 (console viz PR).

Notes / decisions: Use consistent-hash shard key = tenant_id + region to reduce cross-region skew. Quotas are soft (burst tokens) enforced with 429 response; request-level sampling preserves tracing headers for at least 1% of rejected requests for debugging. Will not implement per-tenant storage encryption here — left to Private node-configurations.
